metadata.title: How Does Claude Tell Whether a Bond Is Rich or Cheap?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude judges a bond's richness or cheapness by trading feel, or by running a fixed computed comparison across price, curve, spread, and stress scenario. Lands the carry-out that a rich-or-cheap read is a computed number waiting for a trader's decision, not Claude's own call.

beats.narration_text: Someone asks whether Claude picks a rich or cheap bond by trader's feel, the way a trader might. It doesn't. Liam is here to take you through what the skill actually computes, step by step.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Which bond is rich or cheap -- by feel?', hesitates on 'feel', corrects to 'a curve', lands the real question

props.text:
Which bond is
rich or cheap —
by feel?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('feel' -> 'a curve') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that Claude judges whether a bond is rich or cheap using its own market feel. But the skill doesn't work that way. It computes a relative-value read from four fixed inputs: the bond's price, the yield curve it sits on, the credit spread over that curve, and a stress-tested rate shock. Give it a bond with no yield curve to compare against, and it won't invent one -- there's nothing to spread it against, so there's nothing to read.

shot.new_visual_element: A trader's-feel figure struck through; a priced/curve/spread/stress checklist lit instead

production_viz.label: Feel, struck -- price/curve/spread/stress, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a figure icon labelled 'TRADER'S FEEL' beside a thought-bubble of scattered decision marks. Right: a numbered card labelled 'PRICE / CURVE / SPREAD / STRESS'. The feel side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the procedure side stays lit. A final line reads 'no curve -- nothing to spread it against' and the figure does not reach for it.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does: it combines the bond's price, the yield curve context, and the credit spread over that curve, then runs a stress-tested rate shock across the result. Watch the anchor: a ten-year corporate bond trading forty basis points over the curve. It's priced, the curve is read, the spread is decomposed, and the stress scenario is run. Then it stops -- with a single read, cheap by eight basis points, waiting.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- a ten-year corporate bond traveling priced -> curve read -> spread decomposed -> stress run, then stopping

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one bond, four stops
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'PRICED', 'CURVE READ', 'SPREAD DECOMPOSED', 'STRESS RUN'. A single highlighted token '10Y CORP +40BP' travels down through all four cards in turn, each lighting as it arrives. At the bottom, the token halts beside a label 'read: cheap 8bp -- waiting'. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, PAID OFF, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: That read is built -- priced, curved, spread-decomposed, and stress-tested. But a bond that comes back cheap by the read isn't the same as a bond worth buying: the read only reflects the curve you gave it, and a stale curve makes a wrong read look just as confident. And a bond that comes back rich by the read isn't automatically one to avoid -- the stress scenario can still favor holding it. Either way, the read waits for a trader's decision before anything trades.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, resting at the read; splits into 'cheap is not worth buying' and 'rich is not avoid it'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- read, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, the token resting at the 'STRESS RUN' card beside 'read: cheap 8bp'. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'CHEAP: 8BP' with a checkmark, then a struck-through 'WORTH BUYING?' beneath it, labelled 'cheap is not worth buying'; right reads 'RICH' beside a faint 'stress favors holding' note, labelled 'rich is not avoid it'.

beats.narration_text: A computed rich-or-cheap read isn't Claude's call on what to buy -- it's a number built from price, the curve, the spread, and a stress test, waiting for a trader's decision.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. Give Claude one bond, its price, and a yield curve to compare it against, and ask it to run the bond-relative-value skill: decompose the spread and stress-test it against a rate shock. Then swap in a different curve for the same bond, and watch how much the read moves. Liam, in for Bear.
